title: CypherWave — throughput breakout & hosting path discussion
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2028-06-30 16:00 PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Lin, Victor Gomez, Priya Nair (Redwood) — Ethan Park, Rhea Patel, Jonas Meyer, Lina Santos (CypherWave)

Summary: quick discovery to map p95 targets, concurrency, and streaming/ token-per-sec expectations; evaluate hosted vs dedicated vs private for their real-time summarization product.
Topics: p95 latency targets, concurrency (active dialogs), streaming token/sec, cold start behavior, KV cache strategies, security (SOC2, KMS, SSO), pilot/benchmarks.

00:00 Ethan Park: okay, uh, thanks everyone for joining. we wanted to, like, get a sense of model hosting options. we're leaning toward low latency for our live summarization flow. p95 is critical — sub 350 ms ideally for short responses.
00:18 Maya (AE): great, that's helpful — wanted to confirm that's for the short summarization path? like ~40-80 tokens returned usually?
00:27 Ethan: yes, most responses are 30–60 tokens, but we also have longer context jobs up to 800 tokens for nightly batch.
00:42 Victor (SE): okay that helps. sub-350 ms p95 for 30–60 tokens is doable on the right infra; question is concurrency — how many simultaneous active users?
00:55 Rhea: average concurrent sessions today 1200 active, peak bursts up to ~6k for brief promo spikes.
01:05 Jonas: and our clients expect streaming so they start rendering partial sentences, so token/sec latency matters as well — we need both low p95 and smooth token streaming.
01:18 Priya: streaming adds complexity cause you have sustained token throughput, not just single-shot. what's your target tokens/sec during peak?
01:26 Rhea: peak token emit around 25k tokens/sec across the fleet. average sustained 6–8k.
01:38 Maya: okay, good color. two vectors: single-request p95 and aggregate token/sec capacity. hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs — hosted gives fastest onboarding; dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation; private gives full control but longer setup.
01:55 Lina: security is a hard constraint for some customers — we need KMS integration and regional data residency for EU. SOC2 is baseline. can you confirm Redwood supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs?
02:07 Victor: yes, private and dedicated both can do CMK via KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, and VPC peering. hosted supports encryption at rest and in transit and enterprise plan supports enterprise KMS for some customers — we'll follow up with the security pack.
02:24 Ethan: cost is also big — we can't blow the infra budget. what are typical cost deltas between hosted and dedicated for that token/sec profile?
02:33 Maya: rough rule of thumb: hosted is higher per-token but you get a lot of operational overhead removed; dedicated is better for sustained high throughput. exact numbers depend on model and quantization. we'll propose numbers after we baseline your real token mix.
02:50 Rhea: model question: we plan to use a 13B LLM quantized to int8-ish for latency, with a small reranker. we want to try lower-precision and see quality delta.
03:02 Victor: great — that maps to our optimize recommendations: int8 or q4_0 for tradeoffs. we can run sample benchmarks with both to show p95 and token/sec.
03:15 Jonas: what about cold starts? at a 6k peak, we can't tolerate cold starts on every burst. we need warm pools or instant burst fallback.
03:26 Priya: Redwood Dedicated supports reserved pools and burst capacity to avoid cold starts; hosted has autoscaling with warm warmups but for very spiky workloads we recommend dedicated or private with canary fallback to smaller models for burst.
03:40 Ethan: can you explain the fallback path? we need deterministic SLOs for SLAs with customers.
03:49 Victor: example: primary route on dedicated high-perf model; if capacity strained, policy routes to a quantized variant with slightly higher latency but same API shape. streaming is preserved by seamless model variant swap; you can also route by region for cost vs latency balance.
04:05 Lina: and how do you measure p95? where do metrics live? we need token-level traces and request identifiers for audits.
04:14 Priya: Redwood Console gives per-request token breakdowns, per-model p95, tail latencies, and token attribution. you can export traces to your observability stack and we keep audit logs.
04:27 Ethan: timeline: we're hoping to pilot in 6 weeks, decide hosting mode by exec review in 8 weeks.
04:34 Maya: that's tight but feasible. next steps would be a benchmark run: you provide sample traffic and prompt sets, we run hosted and a dedicated baseline and share results within 10 business days.

04:50 [Discussion — technical details]
05:00 Victor: can you share your average sequence lengths and distribution? we need seqlen histogram to pick batching and kernel profiles.
05:08 Rhea: median 280 tokens of context (we keep conversation history + doc context), input tokens usually 220, output 40. tails up to 1600 during long summaries.
05:21 Victor: okay that explains the batch sizing — large context implies larger KV cache usage. we might suggest prefix caching for repeated docs to cut cost.
05:32 Jonas: what's the impact of prefix caching on streaming?
05:39 Priya: prefix (KV) cache gives immediate warm starts for repeated prefixes — streaming latency on initial tokens is lower. for truly unique prompts you'll still pay the cost. also note the transcript sometimes says KV cash in some docs — minor typos in exports.
05:58 Ethan: what about token burst shaping — can you handle sudden +50% token/sec for 30s bursts?
06:05 Victor: Dedicated with autoscale burst and reserved headroom can absorb that; hosted sometimes needs policy-based throttling or fallbacks to cheaper variants. we'll simulate 30s spikes in benchmarks.
06:18 Rhea: let's talk SLOs — our contract requires 99.95% availability and p95 under 350 ms for the short path. Does Redwood have customers at that SLO?
06:29 Maya: yes, we have enterprise customers hitting p95 ~250–300ms on dedicated for 13B quantized setups. We'll share anonymized references.
06:40 Lina: compliance checklist — SOC2 Type II, ISO27001, SAML SSO, SCIM, KMS, VPC peering, audit logs. can you share the security pack and a self-hosted/private deployment timeline?
06:53 Maya: send security binder. Private deployment typically 8–12 weeks depending on on-prem networking. Dedicated is faster, ~2–4 weeks for capacity provisioning.
07:06 Jonas: operational question — how do we do canary rollouts of new model versions without disrupting p95?
07:14 Victor: Redwood supports canary route splitting by percentage, per-route model pinning, and automatic rollback on quality regressions. You can set SLO gates and automatic fallback.
07:27 Rhea: okay great. a couple of items we want included in the benchmark: end-to-end latency (ingest to first token), p95 for first token and end-of-stream, sustained tokens/sec metrics, and cost-per-1M-tokens estimate for each hosting mode.
07:44 Maya: noted. we'll run: hosted baseline, dedicated baseline with preferred instance types, and a private outline.
07:52 Ethan: to share traffic, we will scrub PII but keep realistic distribution; will that be enough?
07:59 Priya: yes, we only need sequence length distribution, prompt templates, and tokenization artifacts. sample payloads with redacted content are fine.
08:10 Lina: one more — do you support HSM-backed KMS for private? our legal requires HSM for keys.
08:17 Victor: yes, private supports HSM/KMS. we'll add details in the security binder.
08:24 [brief side discussion about benchmarking mechanics — VM types, GPU families]
08:36 Victor: for 13B int8 we'd typically test on A100 80GB equivalent and also an 8-bit optimized path on newer GPUs; quantization matters a lot to p95.
08:48 Jonas: is there an ops runbook for traffic spikes? we want playbooks.
08:53 Maya: Redwood Console includes runbooks and ops playbooks; we'll include a tailored playbook for your thresholds.
09:02 Ethan: how do we measure quality regressions for quantized variants? we need automatic evals on prompt suites.
09:11 Priya: Redwood Optimize can run rolling evals on your prompt set and raise alerts on regression. we'll include sample eval scripts.
09:21 Rhea: what's a realistic dedicated commit level for 6–8k sustained token/sec?
09:28 Maya: initial suggestion: a small dedicated cluster — approximate numbers we'll compute after you give the distribution, but expect dedicated to be cost advantageous after sustained 4–6 weeks at that throughput.
09:41 Ethan: great. last question — is multi-region active-active supported for failover?
09:47 Victor: yes, smart routing can do active-active with regional fallbacks and automatic failover policies. canary by region too.
09:56 [Wrap]
10:00 Maya: recap and next steps — we'll run a benchmark (hosted + dedicated) using your traffic sample, share security binder, cost estimates, and a pilot proposal. propose to schedule demo of the Redwood Console and a follow-up in 10 business days.
10:15 Ethan: sounds good. any blockers on Redwood side?
10:19 Maya: just need sample traffic, seqlen histograms, and exec contact for approval path.
10:26 Jonas: we'll send artifacts by EOD tomorrow.
10:34 Lina: can you include a short note about data retention and log redaction?
10:38 Priya: yes — we'll include retention options and log redaction patterns in the security binder.

Action items in note area:
- CypherWave -> send sample traffic, sequence length histogram, and exec approver contact (Jonas / Rhea) - ETA 2028-07-01
- Redwood -> run hosted baseline & dedicated baseline, produce p95, first-token latency, sustained tokens/sec, and cost delta report - ETA 10 business days
- Redwood -> share security binder (SOC2/ISO/KMS/HSM/SSO details) - ETA 48 hours
- Redwood -> schedule console demo & ops playbook walk-through - propose 2028-07-10

Transcript ends.

Redwood to send security binder and KMS/HSM details
